space:2.en: The message was embedded in the *space* between two audio signals — a narrow silent gap that lasted exactly 0.3 seconds and repeated every minute. Ali had mapped it by chance. Inside that tiny gap lived a set of coordinates, a time, and four words: 'come alone, no wire.'
space:2.cnHint: 讯息藏在两段音频之间的____里，里面是一组坐标和四个字。
space:2.hook: The coordinates pointed to a place I had burned down two years ago.
space:2.line: 'The answer is hidden in the *space* between the signals.'

explain:2.en: A folded note landed on my desk. Grey Crow's handwriting — sharp, urgent. It listed three dead radio towers and a set of numbers I did not recognise. No greeting, no signature. He expected me to work it out alone. But the numbers made no sense until I found the burned circuit board underneath, and then everything clicked. He did not need to *explain*: the board was the key.
explain:2.cnHint: 一张纸条和一块烧毁的电路板让我明白了灰鸦的意图，无需多言。
explain:2.hook: The key opened a door I was never meant to find.

examine:2.en: The signal booth on Deck Nine smelled of cold metal and old fear. Ali held the lantern while I crouched over the console. Someone had been here recently — a coffee ring still damp, a cable cut clean. I began to *examine* every port and wire, looking for the message Zero had hidden inside the machine itself.
examine:2.cnHint: 我在九号甲板的信号亭里仔细____着控制台，试图找出零点藏匿的讯息。
examine:2.hook: Then the console blinked on — by itself.
examine:2.line: '*Examine* the red cable first — trust me on this.'

influence:2.en: Zero never used threats. That was what made him dangerous. He would plant a single word in a broadcast, and within hours a whole district would shift its mood — restless, fearful, ready to act. Grey Crow warned me about this power. 'Words *influence* crowds the way water shapes stone,' he said. I was beginning to believe him.
influence:2.cnHint: 零点用一个词就能____整个街区的情绪，灰鸦早已警告过我这种力量。
influence:2.hook: Tonight, that single word was already spreading.
influence:2.line: 'A quiet word can *influence* a city — never forget that.'

argue:2.en: Ali and I stood in the relay room beneath Pier Twelve, rain hammering the ceiling. She said the signal was a warning. I said it was a trap. We began to *argue* in sharp whispers, our breath misting in the cold air, until a third burst of static cut us both off. The signal had changed while we were fighting.
argue:2.cnHint: 我和阿栗在码头下方的中继室里____起来，争执间信号却悄悄变了。
argue:2.hook: Someone had been listening to every word we said.
argue:2.line: 'Don't *argue* — just read the last line of the code.'

pass:2.en: The checkpoint at Grid Seven was supposed to be closed at midnight. I watched Zero *pass* through it without slowing down — no badge shown, no word spoken. The guard simply stepped aside as if an invisible command had been given. I pressed myself against the wet wall and counted to ten before I followed. Something was very wrong.
pass:2.cnHint: 零点毫不停顿地____了七号检查站，守卫像收到无声命令般让开了路。
pass:2.hook: The guard's eyes were empty — completely blank.
pass:2.line: 'If you can *pass* that gate, you're already in their system.'

serious:2.en: Grey Crow met me on the roof of the old exchange building. He did not look at the city lights. He looked at me — long and level — and I knew this was not a routine briefing. 'The breach is *serious*,' he said at last, setting a data chip on the ledge between us. 'Zero already has two of the four keys.'
serious:2.cnHint: 灰鸦神情凝重地告诉我，这次的安全漏洞十分____，零点已经拿到了四把钥匙中的两把。
serious:2.hook: Two keys left — and Zero knew where they were.
serious:2.line: 'This is *serious* — one more breach and the whole grid falls.'

despite:2.en: The archive room was flooded to my ankles. Cold, black water. Every step sent ripples across rows of drowned filing cabinets. *Despite* the damage, one cabinet stood locked and dry on a raised platform — as if someone had placed it there on purpose, after the flood. Ali's voice crackled in my earpiece: 'That cabinet was moved tonight.'
despite:2.cnHint: ____档案室被淹，有一个文件柜却完好无损地立在台上，似乎是刻意摆放的。
despite:2.hook: The lock bore Zero's signature cut — fresh and clean.
despite:2.line: '*Despite* everything, the file is still here — grab it now.'

express:2.en: The coded graffiti covered the entire east wall of Sub-Station Four. Most of it was noise — decoy symbols. But one line near the floor was different. Whoever left it had used three layers of cipher just to *express* a single idea: someone inside our unit was feeding Zero our routes. I photographed it and said nothing to Ali. Not yet.
express:2.cnHint: 涂鸦中有一行暗语费尽周折只为____一个信息：我们内部有人在向零点通风报信。
express:2.hook: The handwriting matched someone I saw this morning.
express:2.line: 'The only way to *express* it safely was to hide it here.'

career:2.en: The file was thin but heavy with meaning. Grey Crow slid it across the wet table. 'This person built a quiet *career* in data smuggling,' he said. 'Three cities, six years, zero arrests.' I stared at the photo. The face was familiar — too familiar.
career:2.cnHint: 灰鸦出示了一份档案，揭示某人在数据走私领域的____，我认出了照片里的脸。
career:2.hook: The face in the photo was mine.
career:2.line: 'A *career* built on silence always ends in noise.'

medium:2.en: Ali found it wedged behind a loose floor tile — a thin glass disc, the kind used as a *medium* for storing illegal signal patterns. 'This carries encoded voices,' she whispered, holding it to the dim neon light. Outside, rain hammered the alley. Someone had left this here on purpose.
medium:2.cnHint: 阿栗在地板砖下发现了一个用作传递非法信号的____，它似乎是被人故意藏在那里的。
medium:2.hook: The disc began to glow on its own.
medium:2.line: 'This *medium* holds a voice that was erased three years ago.'

office:2.en: The address led me to a grey tower on the east docks. Room 14B was listed as a data broker's *office*, but the door was cold, the lights dead, and the desk empty except for one folded note. I unfolded it slowly. Four words. My own name, misspelled — deliberately.
office:2.cnHint: 我来到一间废弃的____，桌上只留着一张折叠纸条，上面写着我的名字。
office:2.hook: The misspelling was a warning, not a mistake.
office:2.line: 'The *office* was cleaned out an hour before you arrived.'

culture:2.en: The graffiti covered the entire tunnel wall — symbols, glyphs, half-words in seven languages. Grey Crow ran his fingers along one line. 'Zero uses street *culture* as cover,' he said quietly. 'The tags are not art. They are coordinates.' I photographed every mark, hands steady, pulse not.
culture:2.cnHint: 灰鸦解释道，零点利用街头____作为掩护，那些涂鸦其实是坐标。
culture:2.hook: One coordinate pointed directly at City Hall.
culture:2.line: 'Street *culture* is the oldest encryption system in Harbor City.'

college:2.en: The dead drop was inside an old *college* building near the northern wall — abandoned since the signal riots of 2091. Ali picked the lock in four seconds. Inside, chalk equations still covered the blackboard. Tucked behind the eraser tray was a data chip, still warm to the touch.
college:2.cnHint: 废弃的____建筑里藏着一个情报转交点，芯片还是热的。
college:2.hook: Warm chips mean someone left just seconds ago.
college:2.line: 'This *college* was shut down because someone taught the wrong language here.'

value:2.en: Zero's broadcast lasted nine seconds before the city filters killed it. But in those nine seconds he said one thing clearly: 'You know the *value* of what you are carrying.' I had been holding Ali's spare data ring all night without thinking. I looked at it now with new eyes.
value:2.cnHint: 零点的广播点明了我随身携带之物的____，我重新审视手中那枚数据戒指。
value:2.hook: The ring had a second layer I had never opened.
value:2.line: 'The *value* is not in the data — it is in who wants it deleted.'

connection:2.en: Grey Crow drew a line on the damp map, linking three districts. 'The *connection* between the burned relay, the missing broker, and the blank file is not random,' he said. 'Someone is cutting the city's memory, node by node.' The rain outside slowed. The silence felt louder than the storm.
connection:2.cnHint: 灰鸦在地图上画出三个地点之间的____，揭示有人在系统性地抹除城市的记忆。
connection:2.hook: The next node on the map was our safehouse.
connection:2.line: 'Find the *connection* and you find the hand behind all of this.'

story:2.en: The old news archive terminal flickered on when Ali touched it. She scrolled fast, then stopped. 'This *story* was published, then erased within an hour,' she said, reading aloud a headline about a data leak in 2097. I recognised the case number. It matched the file in my coat pocket.
story:2.cnHint: 阿栗找到一篇发布后迅速被删除的____，其中的案件编号与我口袋里的档案吻合。
story:2.hook: Someone had erased the story but forgotten to erase the number.
story:2.line: 'A *story* that gets deleted is the only kind worth reading.'

real:2.en: The data chip Grey Crow slipped me felt cold in my palm. On its surface, a single line glowed: 'The *real* Harbor City lives underground.' I had always thought the neon towers above were the whole truth. Now the floor beneath my feet felt thin as paper.
real:2.cnHint: 灰鸦给我的芯片上有一句话，让我开始怀疑这座城市的____。
real:2.hook: Something below the city was breathing.
real:2.line: 'The *real* map is never the one they hand you.'

talk:2.en: Ali found me crouched behind a cold server rack in Sub-Level Nine. She pressed a folded note into my hand: three words in red ink. No sender. No time stamp. The note said only, 'Stop the *talk*.' Somewhere in these walls, a voice had been broadcasting secrets — and someone wanted it silenced.
talk:2.cnHint: 阿栗交给我一张纸条，警告我停止某种____。
talk:2.hook: The broadcast frequency cut to static the moment I read it.

energy:2.en: The grid room hummed like a living thing. Zero had been here — I could tell by the drained relay banks, each one stripped of its core. 'He feeds on *energy*,' Grey Crow had warned me once. Every stolen watt powered something I had not yet seen. The room smelled of burnt copper and bad intentions.
energy:2.cnHint: 零点洗劫了整个电网室，我意识到他一直在积蓄某种____。
energy:2.hook: A single relay blinked back to life — then spelled out my name.
energy:2.line: 'He doesn't need sleep. He runs on *energy* we can't measure.'

plan:2.en: Ali spread the stolen blueprints across the rain-wet floor of the safe house. Every corridor, every exit, every blind camera — marked in green. 'Zero already has a *plan*,' she said, her voice flat. I studied the paper and felt the cold drop in my chest: the marked path led straight through my apartment block.
plan:2.cnHint: 阿栗展开的蓝图揭示了零点已经制定好了一个____。
plan:2.hook: My own address was circled in red at the center of the map.
plan:2.line: 'A *plan* this clean means someone on our side helped him.'

bear:2.en: The sealed crate in Dock Seven had no label, no lock code, only a stamped warning I almost missed in the low light. Grey Crow knelt beside it and read aloud: 'Contents *bear* no official signature.' That meant ghost cargo — unregistered, untraceable. In Harbor City, ghost cargo never carried anything good.
bear:2.cnHint: 停靠在七号码头的货箱上，有一行字说明其内容____着某种特殊标记。
bear:2.hook: Inside the crate, something shifted and went still.
bear:2.line: 'I refuse to *bear* the cost of a secret I did not choose.'

organization:2.en: The symbol was burned into the wall of the abandoned relay station — a circle split by a single line. Ali went pale the moment she saw it. 'That mark belongs to an *organization* the city officially erased ten years ago,' she said. Erased from records, maybe. But someone had just redrawn their sign in fresh carbon.
organization:2.cnHint: 废弃站内墙上的符号，属于一个早已被城市从档案中清除的____。
organization:2.hook: Ali's hand moved to the door before I could ask why she recognized it so fast.
organization:2.line: 'An *organization* that vanishes on paper never truly disappears.'

opportunity:2.en: The checkpoint guard looked away for exactly four seconds — a gap too clean to be luck. Grey Crow touched my arm. 'This is the *opportunity*,' he breathed. Beyond the gate, a terminal held three years of Zero's movements. Four seconds was enough. I stepped forward before I could think of all the ways it could go wrong.
opportunity:2.cnHint: 哨卡守卫短暂转身，给了我们一个难得的____。
opportunity:2.hook: The terminal screen lit up the moment my fingers touched the panel.
opportunity:2.line: 'Every *opportunity* in this city has a price tag on the back.'

professor:2.en: The lecture hall had been empty for a decade, dust thick on every seat. Yet on the main screen, a looping message ran in bright white letters: 'Ask the *professor* what Zero owes him.' No name. No class number. Grey Crow had mentioned only one academic who ever taught signal encryption in Harbor City — and he had disappeared in 2091.
professor:2.cnHint: 废弃讲堂的屏幕上，一条循环消息要我去找某位____。
professor:2.hook: The message timestamp showed it was sent sixty seconds from now.
professor:2.line: 'The *professor* knew the code before Zero was ever born.'

perhaps:2.en: Deep in the old signal tower, I found a folded note tucked behind a cracked wall panel. The ink was faded, but one line was clear: 'Meet me where the city forgets its name.' *Perhaps* Grey Crow had left this before going dark. I turned the paper over. A second message — in a different hand.
perhaps:2.cnHint: 我在信号塔里发现了一张纸条，灰鸦____在失联前留下了它。
perhaps:2.hook: The second message named someone I thought was dead.
perhaps:2.line: '*Perhaps* the answer was here all along,' Grey Crow said softly.

video:2.en: Ali pulled me into a narrow service corridor beneath the market. She held up a small device and pressed play. The *video* was short — thirty seconds — shot in a room I recognised as the old customs dock. Zero stood in the frame, holding a drive, looking straight at the camera as if he knew we would watch.
video:2.cnHint: 阿栗给我看了一段____，零点似乎早就知道有人会看到它。
video:2.hook: The timestamp on the video was two hours from now.
video:2.line: 'This *video* is either a warning or a trap,' Ali said.

prevent:2.en: The broadcast cut out at midnight. Grey Crow had told me the blackout was planned — someone high up wanted to *prevent* the encoded message from reaching the lower districts. I found the relay box in a flooded basement, its wires cut clean. Whoever did this knew exactly what they were doing.
prevent:2.cnHint: 有人故意____加密信息传到下城区，中继箱的线路被切断了。
prevent:2.hook: A wet boot print on the floor told me they had just left.
prevent:2.line: 'We have to move now, or nothing can *prevent* a full lockdown,' Grey Crow said.

source:2.en: The coded graffiti on the tunnel wall changed every night, but the style never did — same angle, same pale ink. I needed the *source*: the person writing it, not just the words. Ali traced the paint compound to a shop in Block Nine. The owner had been reported missing three days ago.
source:2.cnHint: 我试图找到隧道涂鸦的____，结果线索指向一名失踪者。
source:2.hook: His last sale was to someone using Zero's known alias.
source:2.line: 'Find the *source* and you find the whole network,' Grey Crow said.

available:2.en: I reached the archive room at the edge of the port. Most of the old city records had been wiped, but one terminal was still *available*, its screen glowing a dull amber. I sat down and searched the name Grey Crow had given me. Three files opened. The fourth was locked behind a code I did not have.
available:2.cnHint: 档案室里只剩一台____的终端，第四份文件被密码锁住了。
available:2.hook: The code request showed someone else had tried it minutes before.
available:2.line: 'This is the only terminal still *available* — use it fast,' Ali said.

customer:2.en: The neon-lit repair shop on Deck Four looked ordinary. I walked in and asked for a battery cell, acting like any other *customer*. The clerk glanced at my wrist — the marked one — and said nothing. He slid a small envelope across the counter with my change. Inside was a key card with no label.
customer:2.cnHint: 我假装成普通____走进修理铺，老板悄悄递给了我一张没有标识的钥匙卡。
customer:2.hook: The key card was still warm, as if someone had just made it.
customer:2.line: 'Every *customer* who asks for a cell gets checked,' the clerk said quietly.

language:2.en: The wall near the east gate was covered in signs — some in city script, some in old code, some in a mix I could not place. Grey Crow called it the *language* of those who had no safe voice: a living record of every warning the city tried to erase. I photographed it all. One symbol repeated nine times.
language:2.cnHint: 灰鸦告诉我，墙上的符号是无声者的____，其中一个符号重复出现了九次。
language:2.hook: The repeated symbol matched the mark on my wrist exactly.
language:2.line: 'Learn this *language* or you will miss what they are screaming,' Grey Crow said.

test:2.en: Ali handed me a small chip and told me to plug it into the next public terminal I found. 'It is a *test*,' she said, 'to see if the network watches this block in real time.' I found a terminal near the east bridge. I plugged in the chip and counted. At seven seconds, every light on the bridge went out.
test:2.cnHint: 阿栗让我做一个____，看看网络是否实时监控这个街区，结果灯全灭了。
test:2.hook: In the darkness, I heard footsteps running toward me.
test:2.line: 'This *test* will tell us exactly how fast they respond,' Ali said.

sign:2.en: The server room smelled of burnt wire. I swept my light across the floor and stopped cold. Scratched into the concrete near the drain was a small arrow — a *sign* that someone had passed through here recently, leaving a trail only a trained eye could read.
sign:2.cnHint: 我在服务器室的地板上发现了一个____，意识到有人刚刚到过这里。
sign:2.hook: The arrow pointed straight toward the sealed emergency exit.
sign:2.line: 'That *sign* was not there yesterday,' Ali said, her voice flat.

feeling:2.en: Ali handed me a data chip no bigger than a fingernail. The moment my fingers closed around it I had a strange *feeling* — not fear exactly, but a deep pull in my chest, like the chip already knew something I did not. I pocketed it fast.
feeling:2.cnHint: 拿到那枚芯片的瞬间，我产生了一种奇怪的____，好像它在等着我。
feeling:2.hook: Then the lights in the archive hall went out, one by one.
feeling:2.line: 'Trust that *feeling*,' Grey Crow said from the shadows. 'It has kept me alive.'

professional:2.en: The lock on the rooftop relay box had not been forced — it had been opened clean, without a scratch. Zero was *professional*, no question. A street thief would have left marks. This person had the right tools, the right training, and zero interest in being found.
professional:2.cnHint: 继电器箱的锁被干净地打开，说明对方非常____，绝非普通人。
professional:2.hook: A single glove lay on the rooftop — one glove, placed there on purpose.
professional:2.line: 'Only a *professional* opens a lock that quietly,' I told Ali.

behind:2.en: I checked the corridor map twice before moving. The data terminal was *behind* a second wall, hidden inside what the building plans called a 'utility space.' No utility space showed on any public record. Someone had built a room that officially did not exist, and wired it to the city grid.
behind:2.cnHint: 数据终端藏在一面假墙____，一个官方记录中根本不存在的房间里。
behind:2.hook: A soft hum from inside told me the machines were still running.
behind:2.line: 'The real room is *behind* that panel,' Grey Crow said quietly.

government:2.en: The files on the terminal were stamped with a seal I recognised: the three-ring mark of the city *government*, issued before the network shutdown of 2091. Documents that old should have been wiped. Someone had kept them alive on purpose, feeding them power all these years.
government:2.cnHint: 终端上的文件带有____的印章，本该早已被销毁，却有人秘密保存至今。
government:2.hook: The oldest file had been opened just six hours ago.
government:2.line: 'If the *government* finds this room,' Ali said, 'we disappear.'

growth:2.en: Grey Crow spread the city map across the floor. He traced a red line through the harbour district, marking each new relay tower. 'Look at the pattern,' he said. The *growth* of the signal network followed the same grid as the old water tunnels — every tower sat above a tunnel junction.
growth:2.cnHint: 格雷·克罗在地图上标出信号网络的____规律，它与古老的水道惊人地吻合。
growth:2.hook: Whatever was travelling through those tunnels was not water.
growth:2.line: 'The *growth* stops here — right under the central archive,' Grey Crow said.

negative:2.en: I ran the chip through the scanner. Every field came back clean — name, date, origin, access level. Ali leaned over my shoulder. 'All *negative*,' she said. But a chip with no data at all is its own kind of answer. Someone had scrubbed it perfectly, and perfect scrubs cost more than most people earn in a year.
negative:2.cnHint: 芯片扫描结果全部____，但阿里提醒我，完全空白本身就是一种线索。
negative:2.hook: One hidden partition remained, locked behind a code I had never seen.
negative:2.line: 'All *negative* — which means someone very careful touched this,' Ali said.

potential:2.en: Zero had left a voice note on the relay, nine seconds long. Most of it was static. But buried at the four-second mark was a single word: my investigator ID. He knew who I was. Grey Crow had warned me that Zero never targets someone without *potential* use — which meant I was now a piece on his board.
potential:2.cnHint: 零点的留言里藏着我的编号，格雷·克罗说零点只会盯上有____价值的人。
potential:2.hook: I had become useful to the wrong person without ever agreeing to it.
potential:2.line: 'Zero sees *potential* in you,' Grey Crow said. 'That is not good news.'

force:2.en: The locked terminal blinked red. I needed that file before Zero wiped it. Grey Crow had warned me: 'Never *force* a sealed port — the system screams.' I forced it anyway. Three encrypted layers cracked open like old glass. The data spilled out, cold and bright, and something else woke up inside the network.
force:2.cnHint: 我强行破解了封锁的终端，数据涌了出来，但网络深处有什么东西也随之苏醒。
force:2.hook: A new signal was already tracing my location.
force:2.line: 'Never *force* a sealed port — the system screams.'

importance:2.en: Ali slid a memory chip across the wet counter without a word. A single line was burned into its surface: 'You don't know the *importance* of this yet.' I pressed it into my reader. Streets of Harbor City hummed below. The chip held one image — a face I recognised from a file marked destroyed two years ago.
importance:2.cnHint: 阿栗交给我一块芯片，上面刻着一句话暗示着某件事的____，而芯片里藏着一张两年前就该销毁的照片。
importance:2.hook: The face in the image was still alive — and watching me.
importance:2.line: 'You don't know the *importance* of this yet.'

sell:2.en: Zero's voice cut through the static on Channel Nine: 'Every word is a *sell*, rookie — someone always pays the price.' I had just broadcast a coded phrase Grey Crow taught me. Now the market was moving. Bid signals flooded the dark net. Someone had bought my words and was already spending them against me.
sell:2.cnHint: 零点警告我每句话都是一次____，而我刚刚播出的暗语已经被人买走，用来对付我了。
sell:2.hook: The buyer's next move hit my screen before I could breathe.
sell:2.line: 'Every word is a *sell*, rookie — someone always pays the price.'

replace:2.en: The graffiti on Level Nine had changed overnight. Someone had scrubbed Grey Crow's signal-mark and moved to *replace* it with Zero's broken-circle glyph. Ali photographed the wall in silence. That single mark controlled three underground relay stations. Whoever owned it now owned the voice of the lower city.
replace:2.cnHint: 有人用零点的标记____了灰鸦留在九层的暗号，而那个标记掌控着整个下城的通讯中枢。
replace:2.hook: Ali's hand was shaking as she lowered the camera.
replace:2.line: 'They didn't erase it — they chose to *replace* it with his mark.'

approach:2.en: Grey Crow's note was short: 'There is only one *approach* to the Archive — through the noise floor on frequency 44.' I tuned my receiver in the back of a dark shop while rain hammered the roof. The noise floor was not empty. It was a corridor, and someone was already walking it toward me.
approach:2.cnHint: 灰鸦告诉我进入档案馆只有一条____，但当我调频时，发现那条路上已经有人朝我走来。
approach:2.hook: Two sets of footsteps echoed where there should have been one.
approach:2.line: 'There is only one *approach* — through the noise floor on frequency 44.'

engage:2.en: Ali touched my arm. 'Don't *engage* with the mirror-signal,' she said quietly. 'It copies your pattern and reports home.' I had already sent one pulse into it before she spoke. The mirror signal pulsed back — identical, precise, and wrong in one small way I could not yet name.
engage:2.cnHint: 阿栗警告我不要____镜像信号，但我已经发出了一个脉冲，回波里有一处微小的异常。
engage:2.hook: That small wrongness was the only clue I had.
engage:2.line: 'Don't *engage* with the mirror-signal — it copies your pattern.'

ensure:2.en: The relay box was buried under three false floors in a dry-goods store on Pier Eleven. I sealed every exit port myself, the way Grey Crow had shown me, to *ensure* the message left only one way. One clean channel. One destination. But when I checked the log, the message had arrived somewhere else first.
ensure:2.cnHint: 我封锁了所有出口以____消息只走一条路，但日志显示消息在到达目的地之前先去了别处。
ensure:2.hook: That unknown first stop changed everything I thought I knew.
ensure:2.line: 'Seal every port to *ensure* the message has only one road out.'

limit:2.en: Zero's broadcast ran for exactly nine seconds before the city censors killed it. Nine seconds was the *limit* the underground hackers called the 'breath window.' I caught four words inside it. Ali said four words were not enough. Grey Crow said four words from Zero were always too many.
limit:2.cnHint: 零点的广播被审查系统掐断，九秒是____，我只截到了四个词，但灰鸦说零点的四个词已经足够危险。
limit:2.hook: I played those four words again and heard a fifth, hidden beneath.
limit:2.line: 'Nine seconds is the *limit* — they call it the breath window.'

save:2.en: Inside a flooded server room beneath Dock Nine, I found a cracked data chip. Grey Crow had warned me: once the city grid failed, every record would vanish. I had seconds to *save* the encrypted file before the water reached the machine. My hands shook. The upload bar crawled.
save:2.cnHint: 在被水淹没的服务器室里，叙述者拼命将加密文件____下来。
save:2.hook: The bar hit ninety-nine percent — then the lights died.
save:2.line: '*Save* the file first; ask questions after,' Grey Crow said.

service:2.en: The public *service* terminal on Level B of Central Station still glowed in the dark. Most citizens never noticed the hidden input slot below the screen. Ali pressed a folded card into it and stepped back. Somewhere in the ceiling, a camera turned. I pretended to read the transit map.
service:2.cnHint: 在中央车站，阿栗利用一台公共____终端传递了一张折叠卡片。
service:2.hook: The card slot swallowed it — and the screen went blank.
service:2.line: 'This *service* point is Zero's dead-drop,' Ali whispered.

note:2.en: On the mirror of room 407 in the Anchor Hotel, someone had written a single *note* in red marker. The words were ordinary: a time, a floor number, a question mark. But the ink had been mixed with signal dust — only my scanner could read the second layer hidden beneath.
note:2.cnHint: 酒店镜子上的一张____藏着只有扫描仪才能读取的第二层信息。
note:2.hook: The second layer spelled one word: run.
note:2.line: 'Read the *note* carefully — every letter is a digit,' Zero said.

probably:2.en: Ali slid the torn envelope across the table. The sender's address had been burned away, but the symbol pressed into the wax was Grey Crow's mark. 'Zero *probably* intercepted a copy before this reached us,' Ali said quietly. I turned the envelope over. A fine cut ran along the back seam.
probably:2.cnHint: 阿栗推测信件____已被零点截获了一份副本。
probably:2.hook: Inside was a map — with our safe house circled in red.
probably:2.line: 'He *probably* knows where we are by now,' Ali said.

strategy:2.en: Grey Crow drew a thin line across the city map and tapped three points. 'Zero never acts without a *strategy*,' he said. Each point marked a dead signal tower. Together they formed a triangle around the old archive district. Whatever Zero was planning, it would happen at the centre of that shape.
strategy:2.cnHint: 灰鸦分析零点的____，发现三座信号塔围成了一个三角形。
strategy:2.hook: I checked the map's centre — it was our location.
strategy:2.line: 'His *strategy* is to cut every exit before he moves,' Grey Crow said.

building:2.en: The *building* at the end of Marsh Lane had no listed owner, no street number, and no light in any window. Yet every night, data pulses spiked from its roof. Ali had tracked the pattern for a week. Tonight the pulses had stopped. That meant someone inside already knew we were watching.
building:2.cnHint: Marsh Lane尽头那栋神秘____的数据脉冲今晚突然停止了。
building:2.hook: A shadow passed behind the top-floor glass.
building:2.line: 'That *building* is Zero's broadcast core,' Ali said flatly.

community:2.en: The underground *community* called themselves the Clear Signal. They shared no names, only frequency codes. Grey Crow had once been one of them. Now their coded graffiti was appearing on walls across the port district — a warning, he said, not to us, but about us. Someone had told them we were coming.
community:2.cnHint: 地下____"清晰信号"的涂鸦暗示有人已将我们的行踪透露了出去。
community:2.hook: Grey Crow stared at the symbol and said nothing at all.
community:2.line: 'The *community* burns its own members who talk,' Grey Crow said.

internet:2.en: The city's open *internet* had been dark for eleven days. Only licensed nodes could carry data now. Yet Ali's scanner caught a live stream bleeding through a cracked pipe junction under Grid Seven. Someone was broadcasting without a licence — and the voice on the stream was reading my case file aloud.
internet:2.cnHint: 公共____中断已久，但阿栗却在一处管道接口捕获到了一段非法直播。
internet:2.hook: The voice paused, then said my name a second time.
internet:2.line: 'They are using the *internet* blackout as cover,' Ali said.

seek:2.en: The archive room smelled of old wires and cold rain. I moved through rows of dead terminals, searching every dark corner. Grey Crow had told me someone was here before me. I had to *seek* the one file that could prove Zero's network was real.
seek:2.cnHint: 我在档案室里____那个能证明零点网络存在的文件。
seek:2.hook: Then one terminal blinked on — all by itself.
seek:2.line: '*Seek* the red folder, and do not stop for anything,' Grey Crow said.

exist:2.en: Ali pressed her back against the cold server wall. 'Does this network even *exist*?' she whispered. The signal log I held showed ten thousand hidden nodes, each one alive and pulsing. Something vast and invisible had been running beneath Harbor City for years, and nobody had noticed.
exist:2.cnHint: 我们终于找到证据，证明这个隐藏网络真的____。
exist:2.hook: The log then showed one node with my own address.
exist:2.line: 'It does *exist* — I am holding the proof right now,' Ali said.

supply:2.en: Grey Crow met me under the bridge at midnight. He slid a cold metal case across the wet ground. Inside was a fresh battery pack, three signal chips, and a folded map. 'This *supply* should last you two days,' he said, then vanished into the rain before I could ask a single question.
supply:2.cnHint: 灰鸦在桥下给了我继续任务所需的____。
supply:2.hook: The map had a red X I had never seen before.
supply:2.line: 'Take this *supply* and trust nobody else on the street,' Grey Crow said.

visit:2.en: The record showed one quiet *visit* to Lab Seven — logged at 3 a.m., three weeks ago. No name. No badge number. Just a six-digit code that matched the one burned into the wall of my own apartment. Someone had been there, and that someone knew exactly where I lived.
visit:2.cnHint: 实验室记录显示有人在深夜进行了一次神秘的____。
visit:2.hook: The six-digit code began to flash on my screen now.
visit:2.line: 'That *visit* at 3 a.m. was no accident,' Ali said quietly.

worry:2.en: Ali found me staring at the broken transmitter for too long. 'Your *worry* is written all over your face,' she said. She was right. If Zero had already cracked our channel, every message we had sent in the past week was exposed. The whole network could fold before dawn.
worry:2.cnHint: 阿栗看出了我对通讯安全的____，提醒我保持冷静。
worry:2.hook: At that moment my earpiece hissed with Zero's voice.
worry:2.line: 'Put your *worry* aside — we still have one move left,' Ali said.

adapt:2.en: The cipher changed every hour. Most investigators gave up and went home. I stayed. I taught myself to read the new pattern in under four minutes, then in two. Grey Crow had warned me: in Harbor City you *adapt* to the signal, or the signal swallows you whole and moves on.
adapt:2.cnHint: 为了破解每小时变化的密码，我不得不迅速____。
adapt:2.hook: The next shift came forty minutes early.
adapt:2.line: 'You must *adapt* fast tonight — Zero already changed the key,' Grey Crow said.

bit:2.en: The data chip was cracked down the center. I pressed it into the reader anyway. Only a *bit* of the file came through — one fragmented name and a set of map coordinates. It was almost nothing. But in a city full of silence, even one small fragment of truth could light a very long fuse.
bit:2.cnHint: 受损芯片只传输出了____信息，但那已足够危险。
bit:2.hook: The coordinates pointed to the building I was standing in.
bit:2.line: 'Just a *bit* of data got through, but it names someone high up,' Ali said.

check:2.en: I ran the decryption log a second time. Then a third. I needed to *check* every line before I showed Ali the result. One wrong reading and we would chase a ghost for another week. The last line finally resolved. Zero had not sent the signal. Someone inside our own group had.
check:2.cnHint: 我反复____解密记录，结果却指向了内部人员。
check:2.hook: Ali's ID appeared at the very bottom of the list.
check:2.line: '*Check* that line again — I need to be sure before we move,' I said.

stick:2.en: Deep in Sub-Level 9, the maintenance tunnels smelled of rust and old rain. I found a thin data chip, its edge sharp enough to cut. Someone had pressed it into the wet concrete wall so it would *stick* there, hidden in plain sight, waiting for the right pair of eyes.
stick:2.cnHint: 我在地下管道的混凝土墙上发现了一块数据芯片，它____在那里，像是专门留给我的。
stick:2.hook: The chip's seal bore Zero's signature frequency.
stick:2.line: 'It will *stick* long enough for you to read what they buried.'

effective:2.en: Ali spread the signal map across the cracked table. Three routes to the relay tower, three chances to reach Grey Crow. 'The middle path looks clean,' I said. She shook her head. 'Looks are cheap here. Only one route is *effective* — the one Zero hasn't wired yet.'
effective:2.cnHint: 阿栗研究了三条通往中继塔的路线，只有一条是____的，但代价不明。
effective:2.hook: She circled the tunnel marked with a skull in red ink.
effective:2.line: 'Only one move is *effective* now — move before dawn.'

fear:2.en: The broadcast cut in without warning, Zero's voice filling every speaker on Level 6. It named me — my alias, my frequency. Grey Crow had warned me this moment would come. Cold settled in my chest, not *fear* exactly, but something close: the weight of being seen before you are ready.
fear:2.cnHint: 零点的广播突然点出了我的代号，那种沉重的感觉不完全是____，但已经够危险了。
fear:2.hook: My own signal had just become a target.
fear:2.line: '*Fear* is a signal too — don't let Zero read yours.'

hit:2.en: The decryption took eleven seconds. When the final layer broke open, the numbers on the screen *hit* a threshold I had never seen outside training sims — a city-wide blackout code, armed and counting. Ali grabbed my arm. Neither of us spoke. The clock on the wall ticked once.
hit:2.cnHint: 解密结果终于出来，屏幕上的数字____到了一个触目惊心的临界值。
hit:2.hook: We had forty minutes before Harbor City went dark.
hit:2.line: 'When those numbers *hit* zero, there is no second chance.'

assume:2.en: Grey Crow's message was short: 'Don't *assume* the door is locked.' I stood in the corridor outside Lab 7, the keypad dark, the handle cold. I reached out, turned it. The door opened without a sound. Someone had been here — and left in a hurry.
assume:2.cnHint: 灰鸦的留言让我不要____门是锁上的，我照做了，结果令人不安。
assume:2.hook: A single wet footprint led deeper into the dark lab.
assume:2.line: 'Never *assume* the trap looks like a trap.'

generally:2.en: *Generally* the coded graffiti on Level 3 meant nothing — gang tags, dead drops long emptied. But this set was different: seven symbols, fresh paint, placed at exactly my eye level. Ali crouched beside me. 'Someone knew your height,' she said quietly. 'Someone studied you.'
generally:2.cnHint: Level 3的涂鸦____毫无意义，但这次出现的七个符号显然是为我留下的。
generally:2.hook: The last symbol was the one Grey Crow uses to sign warnings.
generally:2.line: '*Generally* I ignore the walls — tonight the walls spoke back.'

interaction:2.en: The city's old traffic grid and the rebel mesh network were never meant to share the same channel. But Zero had forced an *interaction* between them, and the result was bleeding data into every public screen on the boulevard. Faces. Names. Secrets that could get people killed before morning.
interaction:2.cnHint: 零点强行制造了两个网络之间的____，导致大量私密数据泄露到公共屏幕上。
interaction:2.hook: My own file was three screens away and closing fast.
interaction:2.line: 'One *interaction* between those two grids and the city burns.'

top:2.en: The elevator stopped two floors short. I took the stairs, climbing until the door at the *top* opened onto a rooftop soaked in neon rain. A small metal box sat at the centre, bolt-locked, address unknown. Grey Crow's voice came through my earpiece: 'Don't open it alone.'
top:2.cnHint: 我爬到楼梯____，发现雨中的屋顶上放着一个来历不明的金属盒子。
top:2.hook: The box was ticking — not like a clock, like a heartbeat.
top:2.line: 'Meet me at the *top* before Zero gets there first.'

easily:2.en: The server room sat beneath the old fish market, three levels down. Ali found the access panel and popped it open. Inside, a blinking drive held Zero's entire contact list. 'This was *easily* the most exposed cache I have ever seen,' Ali said, voice flat. Someone had wanted us to find it.
easily:2.cnHint: 阿栗在鱼市地下发现了零点的联系人数据，整个数据缓存____ 就暴露在那里。
easily:2.hook: A trap this obvious could only mean one thing.
easily:2.line: 'This was *easily* the most exposed cache I have ever seen.'

protect:2.en: Grey Crow handed me a thin foil sleeve the size of a playing card. 'Slide your badge inside,' he said. 'It will *protect* the signal from being cloned within a twenty-metre radius.' I slid it in. Down the corridor, a scanner beeped twice and went silent.
protect:2.cnHint: 灰鸦给了我一个特殊的套子，用来____我的徽章信号不被复制。
protect:2.hook: The scanner had already logged my position.
protect:2.line: 'It will *protect* your signal from anyone within range.'

advantage:2.en: Zero had chosen the rooftop relay station for a reason. The height gave a clear line to every broadcast tower in the harbour district. 'He holds every *advantage* up there,' I said to Ali. 'Sight, signal, escape route.' Ali checked her device and said nothing. That silence told me enough.
advantage:2.cnHint: 零点占据了屋顶中继站，在那里拥有各种____，阿栗的沉默令我不安。
advantage:2.hook: We had maybe four minutes before he broadcast everything.
advantage:2.line: 'He holds every *advantage* — sight, signal, and a clear way out.'

break:2.en: The transmission had run without pause for eleven hours. Then, at 03:17, there was a *break* of exactly nine seconds. Grey Crow replayed it three times. 'That gap is not a fault,' he said. 'It is a signature.' I leaned in. Someone had signed their name in silence.
break:2.cnHint: 连续播报中出现了一段九秒的____，灰鸦认为那是某人的身份标记。
break:2.hook: The signature matched a frequency we thought was dead.
break:2.line: 'That *break* of nine seconds — someone put it there on purpose.'

conclude:2.en: I spread the three intercepted messages across the table and read them in order. Each one pointed to the same drop point: Pier 9, low tide, no lights. 'What do you *conclude*?' Grey Crow asked from the doorway. 'That Zero is not hiding anymore,' I said. 'He is inviting us.'
conclude:2.cnHint: 我分析了三条截获的信息，从中____出零点其实是在主动邀请我们前往9号码头。
conclude:2.hook: An invitation from Zero was never just an invitation.
conclude:2.line: 'What do you *conclude* from these three messages?'

figure:2.en: Ali pulled the city census record and filtered by known aliases. One *figure* stood out: a registered signal technician with no home address and fourteen different work sites, all within two blocks of Zero's last known locations. I circled the name. Grey Crow nodded slowly. We had a face.
figure:2.cnHint: 阿栗从普查记录中筛选出一个关键____，这个人与零点的活动地点高度重合。
figure:2.hook: The technician's last logged shift ended an hour ago.
figure:2.line: 'One *figure* in this data connects every site on the map.'

fit:2.en: The stolen keycard did not *fit* the lock on the first try. I flipped it, tried again, and felt the mechanism give. The door opened onto a narrow room lined with shelves of coded ledgers. Ali exhaled behind me. Every ledger was stamped with Zero's mark. We had his records.
fit:2.cnHint: 偷来的门卡终于____上了锁，里面的账本全都盖着零点的印记。
fit:2.hook: One ledger was dated three days from now.
fit:2.line: 'The card did not *fit* at first — but the room was worth it.'

particular:2.en: Grey Crow said most couriers could be followed and turned. But this *particular* courier had never once broken his route in four years, not for weather, not for raids, not for anything. 'That kind of discipline means he is protected from above,' Grey Crow said. 'Touch him carefully, or not at all.'
particular:2.cnHint: 这个____的信使四年从未改变路线，灰鸦警告我们要谨慎行事。
particular:2.hook: Protected from above — but by whom, exactly?
particular:2.line: 'This *particular* courier has never broken his route once in four years.'

fruit:2.en: The abandoned market stall held a single plastic crate. Inside, arranged too neatly, lay seven pieces of *fruit* — each one carved with a micro-glyph. Ali spotted the pattern first: the glyphs spelled a dead drop address. Someone had planned this delivery long before we arrived.
fruit:2.cnHint: 阿栗在废弃摊位的____上发现了隐藏的字符，指向一个秘密地点。
fruit:2.hook: The address pointed straight to Zero's last known hideout.
fruit:2.line: 'This *fruit* is a map,' Ali said, voice barely above a whisper.

waste:2.en: Grey Crow's signal came through a cracked public terminal near the flooded underpass. 'Don't *waste* the next ten seconds,' the voice said. A file began uploading to my device — encrypted, heavy, dangerous. Around me, neon reflections rippled across the black water. I grabbed the file and ran.
waste:2.cnHint: 引路人警告我不要____时间，一个危险文件正在悄悄传输过来。
waste:2.hook: The file's first line read: 'They already know you're here.'
waste:2.line: 'Do not *waste* these seconds — move now,' Grey Crow ordered.

learning:2.en: The hidden library beneath Pier Nine smelled of salt and old circuits. Rows of data chips lined the shelves — decades of stolen *learning*, copied from universities before the Signal Ban. Ali ran a finger along one row. 'This is what Zero is after,' she said quietly. 'All of it.'
learning:2.cnHint: 码头地下图书馆里存放着被禁止的____，而这正是零点的目标。
learning:2.hook: One shelf was already empty, its dust outline still fresh.
learning:2.line: 'Stolen *learning* is still power,' Ali said, eyes scanning the shelves.

manager:2.en: The detention log listed only one name with clearance to enter sublevel four: a *manager* from Harbor City's Signal Authority, registered under a false address. Grey Crow had flagged the name three weeks ago. Now that same name appeared on the crate we found in the market. The link was real.
manager:2.cnHint: 一位信号局____的名字出现在档案和货箱上，两条线索汇成一处。
manager:2.hook: Grey Crow's next message said only: 'He's still inside the building.'
manager:2.line: 'That *manager* signed every illegal transfer,' Grey Crow said flatly.

knowledge:2.en: Zero left a single data chip taped beneath the bridge railing. I played it through my earpiece. A recorded voice listed names, dates, coordinates — raw *knowledge* that could collapse three city districts' worth of cover stories. My hands were steady. My mind was not. I kept walking.
knowledge:2.cnHint: 零点遗留的芯片里藏着足以动摇整个城区的____，我独自听完了它。
knowledge:2.hook: The last name on the list was mine.
knowledge:2.line: 'This *knowledge* is a weapon,' the recorded voice said, calm and cold.

mental:2.en: The interrogation room in Sub-station Eleven had no windows. Grey Crow had warned me about this place — the silence was a tool, designed to increase *mental* pressure until a person simply started talking. I counted the rivets on the opposite wall. Forty-one. I said nothing. The door stayed shut.
mental:2.cnHint: 审讯室的死寂是一种____施压手段，我默默数着墙上的铆钉撑过去。
mental:2.hook: Then the lights cut out, and someone sat down across from me.
mental:2.line: 'The silence is *mental* pressure — they want you to break,' Grey Crow had warned.

weight:2.en: The data core was smaller than my fist but felt wrong in my coat pocket — a strange, quiet *weight* that made every step feel noticed. I crossed the checkpoint bridge with my eyes forward. The guard scanned my badge. One second. Two. The light turned green. I kept breathing.
weight:2.cnHint: 装着数据核心的口袋有种异样的____，我屏住呼吸走过了检查站。
weight:2.hook: Behind me, I heard the guard pick up a radio.
weight:2.line: 'You feel that *weight*? That means it matters,' Ali said.

academic:2.en: The broadcast was formatted to look like a dry *academic* paper — footnotes, numbered sections, a fake university seal. But buried in the citations was a live frequency. Grey Crow had taught me to read this way. I found the frequency on line forty-seven and tuned in. Zero was already speaking.
academic:2.cnHint: 那份伪装成____论文的广播里藏着一个实时频率，零点的声音正在播出。
academic:2.hook: Zero's first words were: 'I knew you would find this.'
academic:2.line: 'It looks *academic*, but every footnote is a coordinate,' Grey Crow said.

major:2.en: The old data-vault beneath the night market held ghost files no one was supposed to find. Ali pressed her palm to the cold door. 'There is a *major* problem,' she said. The vault log showed three hundred deleted names — each one a missing person case the city had quietly buried.
major:2.cnHint: 地下数据库里的记录揭示了一个____的问题：三百个失踪案被秘密掩盖。
major:2.hook: Every deleted name had the same last timestamp: tonight.
major:2.line: 'There is a *major* problem — three hundred names, all erased tonight.'

communication:2.en: Grey Crow handed me a small copper chip no wider than a fingernail. 'Standard *communication* between Zero's people runs through this,' he said. I held it up to the neon light. The chip pulsed once, faint and slow, like a heartbeat that was not supposed to be there.
communication:2.cnHint: 灰鸦交给我一枚铜芯片，说零点团伙的____都靠它传递。
communication:2.hook: The pulse came again — and this time it spelled my name.
communication:2.line: 'All *communication* between Zero's people runs through this chip.'

market:2.en: The floating *market* above Sector Nine sold things the law could not name. I moved through the crowd, hood low, scanning faces. Ali had said to look for a red lantern with no flame. I found it swinging above a stall that sold only silence — and beneath it, a sealed envelope with my badge number on it.
market:2.cnHint: 我在九区的空中____找到了一个挂着红灯笼的摊位，摊位下藏着写有我证件号的信封。
market:2.hook: Inside the envelope was a map — and it ended at my own door.
market:2.line: 'The *market* above Sector Nine — that is where the drop is made.'

apply:2.en: The message was written in heat-ink, invisible until warm. Grey Crow told me to *apply* steady breath to the paper, slow and close. I leaned in. Letters rose like frost burning off glass: six coordinates and one word — RUN. My hands stayed still. My pulse did not.
apply:2.cnHint: 灰鸦让我把呼吸____在纸上，隐藏的字迹才会浮现。
apply:2.hook: The last coordinate was the building I was standing in.
apply:2.line: '*Apply* your breath to the paper — steady, or the ink burns away.'

per:2.en: Zero's network charged one favour *per* secret shared — never money, always leverage. Ali had found the rate sheet cached in a broken street terminal. Each line was a name, a secret, a price. Line forty-seven was mine. I had never told anyone that secret. Someone had sold it anyway.
per:2.cnHint: 零点的网络每泄露一个秘密就收取一个人情作为代价，____个秘密____个人情，第四十七行写的是我的名字。
per:2.hook: Line forty-seven had been sold three days before I joined the investigation.
per:2.line: 'One favour *per* secret — that is Zero's only rule.'

treat:2.en: The city's welfare board claimed to *treat* every citizen as equal under the law. The document Ali pulled from the archive told a different story: residents of Sector D received half the services, twice the surveillance. Someone had signed off on it. The signature was Grey Crow's old captain.
treat:2.cnHint: 福利局声称____每位市民一律平等，但档案里的文件揭露了截然不同的真相。
treat:2.hook: The signature was dated the same week Grey Crow disappeared the first time.
treat:2.line: 'They claim to *treat* every citizen equally — the archive proves otherwise.'

creative:2.en: Zero's coded graffiti had always seemed random to the patrol units. But Ali saw it differently. 'Whoever does this is *creative*,' she said, tracing the loops and dashes. 'It is not art — it is a living map, updated every night.' She stepped back. A new symbol had appeared while we watched.
creative:2.cnHint: 阿栗认为零点手下涂写密语涂鸦的人非常____，那些图案其实是每晚更新的活地图。
creative:2.hook: The new symbol pointed directly to the precinct's evidence room.
creative:2.line: 'Whoever codes these walls is *creative* — and updating them right now.'

perform:2.en: The terminal asked me to *perform* a three-step identity check before it would release the file. I entered the code Grey Crow had given me. Step one cleared. Step two cleared. On step three the screen went dark, and a new voice — calm, unhurried, unmistakably Zero's — said: 'Thank you for the access.'
perform:2.cnHint: 终端要求我____三步身份验证才能调取文件，但第三步完成后，零点的声音出现了。
perform:2.hook: The file was already gone, and the exit doors had just locked.
perform:2.line: '*Perform* all three steps — or the file destroys itself in sixty seconds.'

consequence:2.en: Deep in the transit archive, I found a sealed file tagged with Zero's code name. The data inside listed names — people who had asked too many questions. Grey Crow had warned me: every choice in Harbor City carries a *consequence*. I stared at my own name, third from the top.
consequence:2.cnHint: 我在档案库里发现了一份封存文件，上面赫然出现了自己的名字，令我意识到此事的____。
consequence:2.hook: Someone had already marked me before I found them.
consequence:2.line: Grey Crow said, 'Every *consequence* here is written before the choice is made.'

realize:2.en: Ali slid a cracked data chip across the wet table without a word. I turned it over in my fingers — standard issue, nothing odd. Then I saw the micro-stamp on the edge. I began to *realize* that this chip had passed through the evidence locker I had sealed myself, three nights ago.
realize:2.cnHint: 阿栗交给我一块数据芯片，我仔细端详后才____它曾出现在我亲手封存的证物柜里。
realize:2.hook: The seal on that locker had never been broken — officially.
realize:2.line: Ali whispered, 'Do you *realize* who else has touched this chip?'

mostly:2.en: The coded graffiti on Pier Nine was *mostly* noise — random letters sprayed to confuse street scanners. But three symbols near the drain pipe were different: sharp, deliberate, recent. Grey Crow had taught me that real messages hide inside the ordinary. I photographed the three symbols and ran.
mostly:2.cnHint: 九号码头的涂鸦____是干扰视线的噪音，但其中三个符号暗藏真正的信息。
mostly:2.hook: The paint was still wet — whoever left it had just gone.
mostly:2.line: Grey Crow told me, 'The signal is *mostly* hidden in what looks like nothing.'

exactly:2.en: The signal pulse came at midnight, *exactly* — not a second early or late. In a city where broadcasts drift and clocks are hacked, that kind of precision meant only one thing: Zero was sending a message directly to me. I checked my scanner. The source was inside the building I was standing in.
exactly:2.cnHint: 信号在午夜____准时抵达，这种精度意味着零点是在专门对我发送消息。
exactly:2.hook: The source was one floor above my head.
exactly:2.line: Zero's voice cut through static: 'I am *exactly* where you are afraid to look.'

vary:2.en: Grey Crow spread six intercepted signal logs across the floor. 'Watch the timing,' he said. Normal city broadcasts *vary* by several seconds — interference, load, weather. These six logs showed zero variation. Someone was running a private, controlled channel, hidden inside the public noise grid.
vary:2.cnHint: 灰鸦指出，这六条截获信号的时间间隔毫无____，说明有人藏着一条私密频道。
vary:2.hook: A controlled channel in Harbor City means someone owns the silence.
vary:2.line: Grey Crow said, 'Normal signals *vary* — these do not, and that is the problem.'

brain:2.en: The small device Ali pulled from the wall panel looked like a fuse. It was not. Grey Crow crouched close and said it was a *brain* tap — something that records thought-pattern signals from anyone who stands within two metres of it. Someone had been mapping our thinking for days.
brain:2.cnHint: 阿栗从墙板里取出一个装置，灰鸦认出那是一个能记录思维信号的____窃听器。
brain:2.hook: Everything we had planned in this room was already known.
brain:2.line: Grey Crow said quietly, 'Someone used this to map your *brain* without you knowing.'

stress:2.en: The message on the dead screen was only eight words, but the font size on two of them was slightly larger. Ali noticed first. 'Visual *stress*,' she said — a technique from old print codes, where emphasis marks the real instruction buried in plain text. The two large words read: LEAVE NOW.
stress:2.cnHint: 死机屏幕上有条八字消息，阿栗发现其中两个词的字体带有视觉____，拼在一起是一道隐藏指令。
stress:2.hook: We had been reading the wrong words the whole time.
stress:2.line: Ali said, 'The *stress* on these two words is not an accident — read only them.'

financial:2.en: The document Grey Crow handed me looked like a routine port report. But the *financial* records inside it showed a pattern: the same sum moved on the same date every month, routed through seven shell accounts before vanishing. Zero was not just a signal hacker. Zero was being paid by someone very powerful.
financial:2.cnHint: 灰鸦给我看的港口报告里，____记录揭示了零点每月定期收到来源神秘的大笔款项。
financial:2.hook: The last transfer was dated yesterday — to an account I recognised.
financial:2.line: Grey Crow said, 'Follow the *financial* trail and you will find who Zero truly works for.'

prepare:2.en: The abandoned print shop smelled of old ink and cold rain. Grey Crow handed me a small data chip. 'You have one hour,' he said. I had to *prepare* a fake identity file before Zero's scanners swept the block. Every second counted.
prepare:2.cnHint: 我必须在零点的扫描器到来前____好一份假身份文件。
prepare:2.hook: The scanner pulse was already two streets away.
prepare:2.line: '*Prepare* the file now, or we lose the window.'

workplace:2.en: The message led me to a flooded office tower on Dock Street. This had once been Zero's *workplace* — rows of dead screens, cracked chairs, cables hanging like dead vines. Someone had left a fresh envelope on the only clean desk. It had my name on it.
workplace:2.cnHint: 我在零点废弃的____里发现了一封写着我名字的信封。
workplace:2.hook: Inside was a photograph I never expected to see.
workplace:2.line: 'His old *workplace* still holds his secrets — look harder.'

post:2.en: Ali found a coded notice on the gray wall of the subway tunnel. 'Someone *posted* this an hour ago,' she said, her light moving over the wet letters. The words formed a warning: stay off Line Nine tonight. We had a train to catch on Line Nine.
post:2.cnHint: 阿栗在地铁隧道墙上发现了一条有人____的神秘警告。
post:2.hook: Our train was already pulling into the station.

measure:2.en: The hidden room beneath the bookshop was smaller than I expected. Ali began to *measure* the walls with a thin wire tool, tapping at each panel. 'The outside does not match the inside,' she whispered. One wall was false. Something was behind it.
measure:2.cnHint: 阿栗用工具____墙壁，发现了内外尺寸不符的秘密。
measure:2.hook: Behind the false wall came a very slow, very cold sound.
measure:2.line: '*Measure* the east wall again — the numbers are wrong.'

recommend:2.en: Grey Crow's voice came through static on my earpiece. 'I *recommend* you leave the building before the third bell,' he said. His tone was flat, which meant he was serious. I had not yet found the file. I had not yet found a way out either.
recommend:2.cnHint: 灰鸦通过耳机____我在第三声钟响前离开大楼。
recommend:2.hook: The first bell rang before I reached the stairs.
recommend:2.line: 'I strongly *recommend* you trust no one in that room.'

resource:2.en: The server room was nearly empty. Someone had stripped it clean — drives pulled, cables cut, even the backup power gone. Ali stared at the bare racks. 'Every *resource* has been removed,' she said. Zero had been here first. He had left us nothing to work with.
resource:2.cnHint: 零点已将服务器房间里的所有____洗劫一空。
resource:2.hook: But one small drive still blinked red in the corner.
resource:2.line: 'Without a *resource* like this, we are running blind.'

specific:2.en: The note from Zero was short and cold. It listed three streets and two times but gave no names. Grey Crow read it twice. 'He is never *specific* without a reason,' he said. Each detail was a trap or a test. We had to decide which before we moved.
specific:2.cnHint: 零点的字条措辞____，灰鸦认为每个细节都是陷阱或测试。
specific:2.hook: We had less than twenty minutes to decide which one it was.
specific:2.line: 'Be *specific* — which corner, which time, which door?'

trouble:2.en: The archive room smelled of rust and old rain. I found the folder Grey Crow had marked — three red lines, no name. Inside: a single photo, a dock, a number. Someone had gone to great *trouble* to hide this, yet left just enough for me to find it.
trouble:2.cnHint: 我在档案室发现了格雷·克劳留下的神秘文件夹，里面只有一张照片和一串数字，有人费尽____把它藏起来。
trouble:2.hook: The dock in the photo — I had walked past it this morning.
trouble:2.line: 'Someone went to great *trouble* to make sure you found exactly this,' Grey Crow said.

reflect:2.en: The data chip sat in a puddle on the subway floor. Its surface seemed to *reflect* something more than the neon above — patterns, shifting, almost like code. Ali crouched beside me, breathing hard. Nobody else on the platform moved. The chip had not fallen. It had been placed.
reflect:2.cnHint: 地铁站台地上的芯片表面____出奇异图案，阿里和我意识到它是被人故意放置的。
reflect:2.hook: The patterns on the chip matched the graffiti on Pier Nine.
reflect:2.line: 'Look — the surface *reflects* a signal, not light,' Ali whispered.

attend:2.en: The message said: *attend* the roof meeting at midnight, Level 40, east tower. No sender. Grey Crow had warned me about meetings with no names behind them. I checked my scanner — the signal was clean, too clean. Ali was already at the door, coat on, waiting.
attend:2.cnHint: 我收到一条匿名消息，要我____午夜的屋顶会面，格雷·克劳曾警告过我这类会面的危险。
attend:2.hook: Someone already knew I would say yes before I decided.
attend:2.line: 'You should not *attend* alone — Zero will be watching,' Grey Crow said.

belief:2.en: Zero left a note folded inside the broken vending machine near Gate Seven. Four words: 'Your *belief* is wrong.' I stared at them under the cold white light. Ali read over my shoulder and said nothing. Whatever I thought I knew about the cipher key — Zero had just cracked it open.
belief:2.cnHint: 零点在自动贩卖机里留下一张纸条，四个字否定了我对密钥的____，让我陷入沉默。
belief:2.hook: If my belief was wrong, every step I had taken was a trap.
belief:2.line: 'Your *belief* in that key will get us both caught,' Zero said coldly.

carry:2.en: Ali found the drive taped under a bench at the night market. Small, black, no label. 'I will *carry* it,' she said, and slipped it into her jacket before I could argue. The crowd pressed around us, steam rising from the food stalls. Somewhere behind, a shadow kept our pace.
carry:2.cnHint: 阿里在夜市长椅下发现了一个无标识的硬盘，坚持由自己____它，但我们身后出现了跟踪者。
carry:2.hook: The shadow stopped only when we stopped.
carry:2.line: 'Let me *carry* it — if they search you, it is over,' Ali said.

else:2.en: The locker held a coat, a key card, and a note in Grey Crow's handwriting: 'Tell no one *else*.' That was all. The key card showed a floor number I did not recognize. Ali checked the building map on her wrist screen and went quiet. The floor did not exist on any public record.
else:2.cnHint: 格雷·克劳的字条叮嘱我不要告诉____任何人，而那张门卡上的楼层在公开记录中根本不存在。
else:2.hook: A floor that does not exist is the safest place to hide something.
else:2.line: 'Do not tell anyone *else* — not even Zero's people know this place,' Grey Crow said.

perhaps:1.en: Rain hammered the neon-lit street. I stood at the corner of Dock Row, scanning coded graffiti on the wall. Each symbol felt like a locked door. *Perhaps* the spray-painted crow near the drain was not random street art — it matched the signal pattern I had heard in my head all morning. I pulled out my scanner.
perhaps:1.cnHint: 我在街角发现一处涂鸦，觉得它____不是随机之作，于是拿出扫描仪。
perhaps:1.hook: The scanner beeped once — then went completely silent.
perhaps:1.line: '*Perhaps* that mark on the wall is the message we have been waiting for,' said Grey Crow.

complete:2.en: Ali slid a folded paper across the wet table. On it, a grid of symbols — half the code we had been hunting for weeks. 'The other half is carved into the east wall of the old signal tower,' she said. Together, the two halves would *complete* the map to Zero's hidden broadcast node. I stared at the paper. Someone had already torn the corner off.
complete:2.cnHint: 阿栗带来了一张纸，上面有半份密码，与另一半合在一起能____整张地图，但纸角已被撕去。
complete:2.hook: The torn corner was still warm.
complete:2.line: 'These two halves *complete* the map — but someone got here first.'
